intro: Welcome! Today we practise the English sounds Indonesian speakers find hardest: short and long vowels (ship or sheep?), th, v and sh, and the last sound of a word. Clear sounds help people understand you the first time. Warm-up: say 'think' and 'this' slowly — where is your tongue?
teachingNotes: Indonesian has one 'i' sound, so ship /ɪ/ and sheep /iː/ often sound the same. Stress that /iː/ is long with the lips spread (like a smile) and /ɪ/ is short and relaxed. The same contrast exists for good /ʊ/ vs food /uː/.

th does not exist in Indonesian: learners say think as 'tink' (/t/) and this as 'dis' (/d/). Teach the tongue tip lightly between the teeth: /θ/ (think, thank you) with air only, /ð/ (this, mother) with voice.
v is often said as f ('fery' for very): the top teeth touch the lower lip AND the voice buzzes (hand on the throat). sh /ʃ/ is like Indonesian 'sy' in 'syarat': round lips, not s (she is not see).

Final consonants: Indonesian speakers often swallow the last sound (ca' for cat) and say a final b/d/g like p/t/k (bed → 'bet'), as in Indonesian 'abad' sounding like 'abat'. Ask learners to finish every word, without adding an extra vowel ('bed-e').

Describe mouth positions in simple words and use minimal pairs. Keep sentences very short and use no new grammar (only chunks like 'This is…', 'I have…'). Don't teach phonetic symbols beyond /ɪ/, /iː/, /ʊ/, /uː/, /θ/, /ð/, /v/ and /ʃ/.

keyPoints.title: Short and long vowels
keyPoints.explanation: English has short and long vowels. Ship has a short, relaxed /ɪ/; sheep has a long /iː/ with the lips spread like a smile. If you change the length, you change the word.

keyPoints.title: th, v and sh
keyPoints.explanation: For th, put the tip of your tongue between your teeth: /θ/ with air only (think), /ð/ with voice (this). For /v/, the top teeth touch the lower lip and your voice buzzes (very). For /ʃ/, round your lips like 'sy' in 'syarat' (she).

keyPoints.title: Finish the word
keyPoints.explanation: Say the last consonant clearly. Without it, cat can sound like cap or can. A final d stays d (bed), it does not become t (bet).

guidedPractice.prompt: Which word has the long 'ee' sound /iː/: sit or seat?
guidedPractice.hint: The long sound has spread lips, like a smile. It's often spelled ee or ea.

guidedPractice.prompt: Which word starts with the voiced th /ð/ (tongue between the teeth, with voice): think or this?
guidedPractice.hint: Put a hand on your throat: one of the words buzzes.

guidedPractice.prompt: Which word ends with the sound /v/: five or fine?
guidedPractice.hint: For /v/ the top teeth touch the lower lip.

guidedPractice.prompt: Which word ends with the sound /d/: bed or bet?
guidedPractice.hint: In English a final d stays d. Don't turn it into t.

independentPractice.prompt: Which word has the short sound /ɪ/: cheap or chip?
independentPractice.hint: The short sound is quick and relaxed.

assessment.prompt: Listen. Do you hear live or leave? Write the word you hear.
Which word has the long sound /uː/, like in 'food': full or fool? Write it.
Listen. Do you hear tree or three? Write the word you hear.
Listen. Do you hear safe or save? Write the word you hear.

assessment.rubric: Correct: they. 'thank' has the voiceless /θ/; 'day' starts with /d/ = 0.

blocks.text: Indonesian has one **i** sound, but English has two: a **short** /ɪ/ (*ship, sit*) and a **long** /iː/ (*sheep, seat*). For the long sound, spread your lips like a smile and hold it a little longer. The same happens with **oo**: short /ʊ/ in *good*, long /uː/ in *food*.

id.text: Bahasa Indonesia punya satu bunyi **i**, tapi bahasa Inggris punya dua: **pendek** /ɪ/ (*ship, sit*) dan **panjang** /iː/ (*sheep, seat*). Untuk bunyi panjang, tarik bibirmu seperti tersenyum dan tahan sedikit lebih lama. Hal yang sama terjadi pada **oo**: pendek /ʊ/ di *good*, panjang /uː/ di *food*.

blocks.text: Spelling often helps: **ee** and **ea** usually sound long /iː/ (*see, tea, seat*). One **i** between two consonants usually sounds short /ɪ/ (*sit, big, fish*).

id.text: Ejaan sering membantu: **ee** dan **ea** biasanya berbunyi panjang /iː/ (*see, tea, seat*). Satu huruf **i** di antara dua konsonan biasanya berbunyi pendek /ɪ/ (*sit, big, fish*).

blocks.prompt: Which word has the long sound /iː/?
blocks.explain: Tea has ea, a long /iː/. Fish and big have a short /ɪ/.

id.explain: Tea ditulis dengan ea, bunyinya panjang /iː/. Fish dan big berbunyi pendek /ɪ/.

blocks.text: Indonesian has no **th**, so learners often say *tink* for **think** and *dis* for **this**. Put the tip of your tongue **lightly between your teeth** and push air out. For **/θ/** (*think, thank you, bathroom*) there is only air. For **/ð/** (*this, that, the, mother*) your voice buzzes too.

id.text: Bahasa Indonesia tidak punya bunyi **th**, jadi pelajar sering mengucapkan *tink* untuk **think** dan *dis* untuk **this**. Letakkan ujung lidah **ringan di antara gigi** lalu hembuskan udara. Untuk **/θ/** (*think, thank you, bathroom*) hanya udara yang keluar. Untuk **/ð/** (*this, that, the, mother*) suaramu ikut bergetar.

blocks.text: Use a mirror: for th you should see the tip of your tongue. If you can't see it, you are probably saying t or d.

id.text: Pakai cermin: untuk th, ujung lidahmu harus terlihat. Kalau tidak terlihat, kemungkinan kamu sedang mengucapkan t atau d.

blocks.prompt: How do you start the word 'thank'?
options: Tongue tip behind the top teeth, like Indonesian t
Tongue tip between the teeth, push air out
Top teeth on the lower lip
blocks.explain: Thank starts with /θ/: tongue tip between the teeth, air only. Behind the teeth is t; teeth on the lip is f or v.

id.explain: Thank diawali /θ/: ujung lidah di antara gigi, hanya udara. Lidah di belakang gigi adalah t; gigi di bibir adalah f atau v.

blocks.text: **v** is not **f**. For both sounds the top teeth touch the lower lip, but for **/v/** your voice buzzes — put a hand on your throat to feel it: *very, van, seven, five*. Saying *fery* for **very** is a common mistake. **sh /ʃ/** is like **sy** in *syarat* or *masyarakat*: round your lips and push air out: *she, shop, fish*. Don't say **s**: *she* is not *see*.

id.text: **v** bukan **f**. Untuk kedua bunyi ini gigi atas menyentuh bibir bawah, tapi untuk **/v/** suaramu bergetar — letakkan tangan di leher untuk merasakannya: *very, van, seven, five*. Mengucapkan *fery* untuk **very** adalah kesalahan umum. **sh /ʃ/** mirip **sy** di *syarat* atau *masyarakat*: bulatkan bibir lalu hembuskan udara: *she, shop, fish*. Jangan ucapkan **s**: *she* bukan *see*.

blocks.text: The throat test: say *ffff* and then *vvvv* with a hand on your throat. Only /v/ buzzes.

id.text: Tes leher: ucapkan *ffff* lalu *vvvv* sambil memegang leher. Hanya /v/ yang bergetar.

blocks.prompt: Which word starts with the sound /ʃ/?
blocks.explain: Shop starts with sh /ʃ/, round lips. Sea and sock start with /s/.

id.explain: Shop diawali sh /ʃ/, bibir dibulatkan. Sea dan sock diawali /s/.

blocks.text: In Indonesian the last sound of a word is often soft: *bapak*, or *abad* that sounds like *abat*. In English the **last consonant changes the meaning**: *cat* (kucing), *cap* (topi), *can* (kaleng). Say every word to the end: **ca-t, be-d, bu-s**. A final **d** stays d: *bed*, not *bet*.

id.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia bunyi terakhir sebuah kata sering lemah: *bapak*, atau *abad* yang terdengar seperti *abat*. Dalam bahasa Inggris **konsonan terakhir mengubah arti**: *cat* (kucing), *cap* (topi), *can* (kaleng). Ucapkan setiap kata sampai habis: **ca-t, be-d, bu-s**. Huruf **d** di akhir tetap d: *bed*, bukan *bet*.

blocks.text: Finish the sound, but don't add a vowel after it: say *bed*, not *bed-e*.

id.text: Selesaikan bunyinya, tapi jangan tambahkan vokal sesudahnya: ucapkan *bed*, bukan *bed-e*.

blocks.prompt: Which word means 'kucing'? Say the last sound clearly.
blocks.explain: Cat ends with a clear /t/. Cap is 'topi' and can is 'kaleng'.

id.explain: Cat diakhiri /t/ yang jelas. Cap artinya topi dan can artinya kaleng.

blocks.text: People can often guess from the situation, but clear sounds save time — at a café, on the phone or at the office. Practise short phrases you use every day, slowly first and then at normal speed.

id.text: Orang sering bisa menebak dari situasinya, tapi bunyi yang jelas menghemat waktu — di kafe, di telepon atau di kantor. Latih frasa pendek yang kamu pakai setiap hari, pelan dulu lalu dengan kecepatan normal.

blocks.text: Record yourself on your phone and compare with the audio. Slow and clear is better than fast.

id.text: Rekam suaramu di ponsel lalu bandingkan dengan audionya. Pelan dan jelas lebih baik daripada cepat.

suggestedQuestions: How can I hear the difference between ship and sheep?
Where does my tongue go for th?
Why do I say 'fery' instead of 'very'?
Why is the last sound of a word so important?

id.intro: Selamat datang! Hari ini kita berlatih bunyi bahasa Inggris yang paling sulit bagi penutur Indonesia: vokal pendek dan panjang (ship atau sheep?), th, v dan sh, serta bunyi terakhir sebuah kata. Bunyi yang jelas membuat orang langsung paham maksudmu. Pemanasan: ucapkan 'think' dan 'this' pelan-pelan — di mana posisi lidahmu?
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana cara mendengar beda ship dan sheep?
Di mana posisi lidah untuk th?
Kenapa bunyi terakhir sebuah kata begitu penting?
